LESSON: READING SYLLABLES READING

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.7: Reading syllables READING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading syllables READING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we blend letter READING (3 HRS) learners should be able to: in blending sounds to sounds to make syllables?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Read syllables in and out da, ma
2. Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING SYLLABLES READING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading syllables READING helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING SYLLABLES READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read syllables in and out da, ma

What this means
In this part you learn to Read syllables in and out da, ma. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Read syllables in and out da, ma.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading syllables READING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Read syllables in and out da, ma. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading syllables READING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading syllables READING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading syllables READING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Read syllables in and out da, ma)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading syllables READING to a partner. (skill: Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading syllables READING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Read syllables in and out da, ma.
3. Practise this skill: Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading syllables READING from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading syllables READING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Reading syllables READING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we blend letter READING (3 HRS) learners should be able to: in blending sounds to sounds to make syllables?
2. What activities would of class. enhance the learner’s ability to read syllables?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading syllables READING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Read syllables in and out da, ma.
5. Be able to: Demonstrate ability to read • Learners could be syllables in class. encouraged to read syllabuses.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
